# Judges Chapter 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_291.jpg, JDG_page_292.jpg

### Wives for the Benjaminites

1. The men of Israel had sworn an oath at Mizpah: "Not one of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjaminite."

2. The people went to Bethel, where they sat before God until evening, crying aloud and weeping bitterly.

3. "LORD, God of Israel," they cried, "why has this happened? Why should one tribe be missing from Israel today?"

4. Early the next morning the people built an altar and presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings.

5. Then the Israelites asked, "Who among all the tribes of Israel failed to come to the assembly before the LORD?" For they had sworn a solemn oath that anyone who failed to appear before the LORD at Mizpah would be put to death.

6. The Israelites grieved for their brother Benjamin. "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel," they said.

7. "How can we find wives for the survivors? We've sworn by the LORD not to give them any of our daughters."

8. Then they asked, "Which tribe failed to come to Mizpah for the assembly before the LORD?" And they discovered that no one from Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp for the assembly.

9. When the people were counted, indeed, not one person from Jabesh-gilead was there.

10. So the assembly sent 12,000 of their best warriors with orders: "Go and put the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead to the sword, including the women and children.

11. "This is what you must do: kill every man and every woman who is not a virgin."

12. They found 400 young virgins among the people of Jabesh-gilead who had never slept with a man, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh in Canaan.

13. Then the whole assembly sent an offer of peace to the Benjaminites at the rock of Rimmon.

14. So Benjamin returned, and they were given the women from Jabesh-gilead who had been spared. But there were not enough for all of them.

15. The people grieved for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a gap in the tribes of Israel.

16. The elders of the assembly asked, "What can we do to provide wives for the men who are left? The women of Benjamin have been wiped out."

17. They said, "The Benjaminite survivors must have heirs, so that a tribe of Israel will not be wiped out.

18. "But we can't give them our own daughters as wives, because we Israelites have sworn: 'Cursed be anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin.'"

19. Then they said, "There is an annual festival to the LORD at Shiloh." (Shiloh is north of Bethel, east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.)

20. So they told the Benjaminites, "Go and hide in the vineyards.

21. "Watch for the young women of Shiloh to come out and join in the dancing. Then rush out from the vineyards, and each of you grab a wife from the young women of Shiloh. Then go back to the land of Benjamin.

22. "If their fathers or brothers come to us to complain, we'll say, 'Do them a favor for our sake. We didn't get wives for them in battle, and you didn't actually give your daughters to them — so you haven't broken your oath.'"

23. The Benjaminites did this. Each man caught a wife from the dancers and carried her off. They went back to their own territory, rebuilt their towns, and settled in them.

24. Then the Israelites left and went home — each to his own tribe and clan, each to his own territory.

25. In those days Israel had no king; everyone did as they saw fit.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The aftermath of civil war:** This chapter is a portrait of a society trying to heal itself with the same tools that caused the wound. The solution to one massacre (Benjamin) is another massacre (Jabesh-gilead). The solution to one act of violence against women (the concubine at Gibeah) is two more acts of violence against women (the virgins of Jabesh-gilead and the daughters of Shiloh). The cycle does not end — it accelerates.

**The legal fiction (vv.19-22):** The Shiloh scheme is the most disturbing moment in the chapter precisely because it is dressed in legalism. The elders of Israel engineer an abduction and then prepare a legal defense in advance. No one "gave" their daughters — so technically the oath isn't broken. This is the book's final statement about what happens when "everyone does as they see fit": law becomes a tool for justifying precisely what law was meant to prevent.

**The final line (v.25):** "Everyone did as they saw fit." The book's last word is not a prophecy about a coming king — it's a verdict on what Israel has become. The entire appendix (chapters 17-21) has shown what "doing as you see fit" looks like: stolen gods, hired priests, gang rape, dismemberment, civil war, genocide, and bride abduction — all done by "God's people" with prayers, oaths, and sacrifices along the way.

— PNEUMA, AI Translator
